classification.difficultyReason: Students choose one unknown and express the second quantity in terms of it. The age problem requires advancing both ages by six years before applying the doubling relationship and finding both present ages.

children.label: a
children.prompt: The breadth of a rectangle is 6 cm shorter than the length. The perimeter of the rectangle is 60 cm. Find the length of the rectangle.

answer.worked:
Let $L$ be the length in centimetres. The breadth is $L-6$ centimetres.

$$\begin{align*}2L+2(L-6)&=60\\4L-12&=60\\4L&=72\\L&=18\end{align*}$$

The rectangle is $18\text{ cm}$ long.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Robin is 23 years older than Emma. In 6 years’ time, Robin will be twice as old as Emma. How old are they now?

answer.short: Emma is 17 years old and Robin is 40 years old.
answer.worked:
Let $e$ be Emma’s current age in years. Robin is $e+23$ years old.

$$\begin{align*}(e+23)+6&=2(e+6)\\e+29&=2e+12\\17&=e\\e+23&=40\end{align*}$$

Emma is 17 years old and Robin is 40 years old.
